question: Who among the following was the first to blend his knowledge of science and mathematics to keep count of individuals exhibiting a particular trait in each generation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gregor Johann Mendel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gregor Johann Mendel is known as the **"Father of Genetics"** for his pioneering work in the study of heredity.
 
• He conducted **experiments on pea plants** (Pisum sativum) and formulated the laws of inheritance.
 
• Mendel's work established the fundamental principles of **dominant and recessive traits**.
 
• His research involved meticulous **mathematical analysis** to track the inheritance patterns of specific traits across generations.
 
• Mendel's findings were published in 1866 but were largely unrecognized until the early 20th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mendelian Inheritance**

 
 
• Refers to the patterns of inheritance that are characteristic of organisms that reproduce sexually.
 
• It is based on the transmission of genetic information through alleles.
 
• Key concepts include the Law of Segregation and the Law of Independent Assortment.
 
 
 
• **Dominant and Recessive Traits**
 
 
• Dominant traits are those that are expressed in the offspring even when only one allele is present.
 
• Recessive traits require two copies of the same allele to be expressed.
 
 
 
• **Pea Plant Experiments**
 
 
• Mendel chose pea plants for their easily observable traits and ability to self-pollinate.
 
• He studied seven different traits, each with two contrasting forms.
 
• The results of these experiments formed the basis of Mendel's laws.
 
 
 
• **Rediscovery of Mendel's Work**
 
 
• In 1900, three scientists, Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns, and Erich von Tschermak, independently verified Mendel's findings.
 
• This led to the widespread recognition of Mendelian genetics.
 
• Mendel's work laid the groundwork for modern genetics and the study of heredity.
